summary: Configure isolated burst pools and smoothing for hybrid realtime + batch traffic
description: Issue summary: Vectorlytics reported recurring soft 429s affecting low-latency chat endpoints when their nightly bulk embedding jobs start. Impact: Chat users (low latency) intermittently receive 429s for 2–7 minutes during a batch start window; bulk jobs also see queueing. Environment: prod (us-east), enterprise tenant, dedicated pool. Steps to reproduce: 1) Start 200 parallel embedding workers using the /v1/embeddings endpoint with 8 concurrent connections each. 2) While bulk workers ramp, start a synthetic chat session (streaming) to the /v1/chat/stream endpoint. 3) Observe intermittent 429 responses and X-RateLimit headers showing per-tenant token depletion. Logs/Headers: X-RateLimit-Limit: 60000, X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0, X-RateLimit-Reset: 38s. Expected: chat requests should be prioritized and isolated from bulk backfills; bulk should throttle gracefully without causing chat 429s. Actual: tenant-level quota is exhausted because bulk traffic and health probes double-count in short windows, causing chat to be unable to get burst credits. Customer asked: how to configure isolated burst pools, smoothing/refill windows, and best-practice routing/priority setup to avoid user-facing 429s while allowing large nightly jobs.
comments: 2024-11-12 09:14 - Maya (Vectorlytics): We're seeing chat users get 429s exactly when our embedding backfill starts. This is a production outage for several customers. Can support help isolate chat?

2024-11-12 09:30 - Support (Asha Patel): Thanks Maya — collecting metadata. Can you share sample request rates and whether bulk workers reuse the same API key as chat? Also any proxy/load-balancer in front?

2024-11-12 10:05 - Maya (Vectorlytics): Bulk uses the same org API key, runs from a Kubernetes CronJob across 6 pods. Chat clients use per-user short-lived subkeys. No external proxy except our small edge service. Attached snippet of headers above.

2024-11-12 14:02 - Eng (Liam Chen): Initial hypothesis: tenant-level token bucket gets drained by bulk because per-route separation wasn't enabled. Health checks from the bulk coordinator are also producing many small requests that increment per-tenant counters. We'll instrument the rate-limiter counters and suggest config changes (route isolation + burst pool).

2024-11-13 08:41 - SRE (Noah Ortiz): Added temporary mitigation: staggered cron start (+120s jitter) and temporary per-route weight to reserve 25% capacity for chat routes. This brought chat 429s down immediately. Need to apply permanent config change and test.

2024-11-15 11:20 - Support (Liam Chen): Deployed recommended per-route burst pool and smoothing parameters for Vectorlytics. Monitoring shows no further chat 429s during scheduled backfills for 48h. Issue resolved; recommending follow-up tuning and a runbook entry.
investigation_notes: Observed high token depletion spikes aligned with Kubernetes CronJob start times (00:00, 04:00, 08:00 UTC) — bulk workers posted many small embedding requests in parallel.
Rate-limiter metrics (rl.*) show per-tenant token reclaim lag: refill_window_ms configured at 1000ms, causing sawtooth behaviour when many short requests arrive simultaneously.
Connection reuse and HTTP/2 multiplexing caused per-connection accounting anomalies: signed-url callbacks from bulk workers resulted in duplicate preflight counting in edge layer.
Per-route isolation was not enabled on Vectorlytics' Dedicated pool. All routes were aggregated under tenant quota, so bursts from bulk consumed chat credits.

SRE trace (trace-id: rwi-20241112-cc1) shows health-checks from bulk coordinator issuing 3–5 fast status pings per worker; these are non-idempotent in accounting and should be marked background or excluded.
Reproducer: Run 150 parallel curl processes sending 32 concurrent embedding requests each to /v1/embeddings; start a streaming chat request in parallel and watch Remaining drop to zero within 12s.
resolution:
Workaround applied: 1) Staggered CronJobs with randomized jitter to smooth arrival. 2) Temporary route-weight reservation (25%) for chat routes via Console to protect low-latency traffic. Permanent fix implemented on 2024-11-15: a) Enabled per-route burst pools for Vectorlytics and created an isolated burst_pool 'chat-burst' with size=1200 tokens and refill_ms=250; b) Configured smoothing window (refill_window_ms=250) for tenant to reduce sawtooth refill; c) Marked bulk coordinator health probes as 'background' to exclude from tenant accounting. Post-change validation: monitored 48h of scheduled backfills, no chat 429s observed and bulk queueing behaved as expected. Recommended follow-ups: - Add a runbook for 'hybrid workload' customers describing per-route burst pool pattern and sample Console settings. - Consider adding auto-detection telemetry to suggest isolated burst pools when mixed realtime+batch traffic is detected (tracked in INT-4312). Example config snippet applied via Console (replace placeholders):

route: /v1/chat/*
  burst_pool: chat-burst
  priority: high
  reserved_percentage: 25

burst_pool: chat-burst
  size_tokens: 1200
  refill_window_ms: 250
  smoothing: true

Note: We advised Vectorlytics to rotate their bulk job API key into a separate sub-key scoped for background ingest to further reduce cross-counting and to add an exponential backoff on failures. Issue status set to Resolved after 48h confirmation.
